goal: Move msfslogger's required/supported Node.js runtime from 20 to Node 24 LTS (Krypton) by clearing the one real blocker — better-sqlite3's native-addon ABI — while leaving every DB and application behavior unchanged, then flipping .nvmrc, package.json engines, and CI to actually require it. Backend-only plus one devops/tooling phase; docs (README.md, docs/**) are explicitly out of this plan and go through the separate update-docs skill afterward.
frozen_decisions: Set Node.js 24 LTS as the supported and required runtime.
If `better-sqlite3` is replaced, a compatible alternative must be selected and integrated (examples include `sqlite3`, `node:sqlite` when stable and suitable, or another maintained option).
Introduce/adjust a small persistence adapter boundary (if needed) to isolate library-specific calls.
Non-goals: major feature additions unrelated to the upgrade; database schema redesign not required by migration; broad refactor beyond what is necessary to replace incompatible dependencies.
Out of scope: multi-database support expansion; performance tuning unrelated to regression fixes.

Acceptance bar: CI passes on Node 24 for build/lint/test; app runs end-to-end with no functional regressions in DB workflows; `better-sqlite3` is either upgraded with confirmed Node 24 support or replaced with a maintained Node-24-compatible alternative; README/dev docs state the Node 24 requirement.
Tasks are backend-only (src/**, tests/**, agent/**) plus one devops-owned CI/tooling phase; no task may touch docs/** or README.md.
Use backend_sr (not jr) for any task touching the DB adapter/call sites.
Verification for anything that builds/runs happens in a scratch clone, never this checkout (live server on :3000, live flights.db).

dependency_decision.path_description: In-place better-sqlite3 version bump (dependencies + @types only). Same contract at every call site — no adapter, no library swap, no Design step.
evidence: npm view better-sqlite3 versions: current line runs 9.4.3 (pinned) through 12.11.1 and 13.0.3, both published 2026-08-05 — 12.x is a live, maintained branch in parallel with 13.x, not abandoned in favor of it.

npm view better-sqlite3@12.11.1 engines -> { node: '20.x || 22.x || 23.x || 24.x || 25.x || 26.x' } — explicit, first-class Node 24 (ABI/N-API 137) support, confirmed by the package's own engines field, not inferred from an issue thread.

WiseLibs/better-sqlite3 GitHub issues #1382/#1384/#1376 (community reports) confirm 11.10.0 and earlier ship no prebuilt binary for Node 24 (node-v137), which is exactly why this repo's .nvmrc is pinned to 20 today; #1478/openchamber corroborates the fix landed at 12.0.0.

13.0.0 is better-sqlite3's first release on N-API (rewritten binary-loading mechanism, engines >=22, drops Node 20) — newer and riskier than necessary for a repo whose bar is 'preserve all current DB and application behavior'; 12.11.1 keeps the long-proven prebuild-install mechanism and, as a bonus, still supports Node 20 in its own engines range, which is a safety margin during rollout even though this repo is dropping 20.

GitHub discussion WiseLibs/better-sqlite3#1277 (maintainer comment): no breaking API change recalled across the project's history; major version bumps have tracked Node/Electron support drops, not API churn — supports a version bump with zero call-site changes.

Actual grep of this tree (`grep -rln "from 'better-sqlite3'\|require('better-sqlite3')" src/ agent/ tests/`) finds only 3 real source call sites — src/db/connection.ts, src/db/schema.ts, src/backup.ts — not the 5 the task envelope's grep suggested. src/kmlExport.ts and src/auth/password.ts only mention 'better-sqlite3' in comments (kmlExport.ts's own header states it performs no I/O and imports no better-sqlite3; password.ts explains in a comment why it avoided a *second* native addon by using node:crypto scrypt instead of bcrypt/argon2). Neither needs any code change.

The API surface actually used — db.prepare()/.get()/.get()/.all()/.run() with positional and @named binds, db.transaction(fn) (including nested calls across src/db/plannedLegs.ts, groundSessions.ts, etc.), db.pragma() including the two-argument { simple: true } form, db.exec(), the async db.backup() used only in src/backup.ts, and db.open — is unchanged by a 9.x -> 12.x bump per the no-breaking-API finding above; a node:sqlite migration would touch all ~8 files under src/db/ plus tests/helpers/db.ts and would need to reproduce db.backup()'s online-backup semantics and the nested-transaction and named-bind-parameter behavior schema.ts's own migration code depends on, none of which node:sqlite's RC-stage DatabaseSync API has been evaluated against here.

node:sqlite is Stability 1.2 ('release candidate') as of Node 24.15+, not the 'stable' bar the source spec sets as a condition for choosing it over a maintained third-party library — this alone is sufficient to prefer the version bump without needing to catalog every API gap.
dependency_decision.rationale: better-sqlite3 12.11.1 fixes the actual blocker (no Node 24 prebuilt binary) with a version already declaring first-class Node 24 support, no known API break, and no library swap — the cheapest change that meets 'preserve all current DB and application behavior'. node:sqlite is not stable yet and would force a rewrite of every src/db/*.ts file plus the online-backup and nested-transaction logic for no behavioral gain. Design is therefore skipped for this run per the Orchestrator's own rule ('a run that only wires up existing contracts skips this step') — nothing here introduces or changes a contract.

excluded_scope.agent/: agent/package.json's only dependency is node-simconnect@4.2.0 (engines >=20.17.0, npm >=10.0.0; pure-JS deps: debug, ini, regedit — no native addon, no better-sqlite3). >=20.17.0 already includes Node 24, so no dependency change is needed there. agent/README.md tells the operator to install 'Node.js 20 LTS' — that's a doc-only statement and falls under the same docs/README exclusion as the root README, not a code change; it's out of scope for this plan.
excluded_scope.docs_and_readme: README.md line 19-20 ('Node.js 20 (pinned by .nvmrc...)') and any agent/README.md wording need updating to say 24, but per project convention no implementer role owns docs/**/README.md — that update is out of scope for plan.json and goes through the update-docs skill once this run's code/CI tasks are reviewed.

sequencing_rationale: Dependency compatibility must be proven under a real Node 24 before the repo's own default flips to it: bumping .nvmrc first would make every subsequent `nvm use` and every CI run (node-version-file: .nvmrc) resolve to a Node 24 whose better-sqlite3 build was never validated — if the bump were subtly wrong, the whole repo would be broken by the same commit that was supposed to prove it worked. Phase 1 verifies the dependency explicitly under `nvm use 24` (or `nvm install 24` first, since only 20 and 26 are installed on this machine per ENVIRONMENT.md) in a scratch clone, before anything in the checkout's own toolchain configuration changes.

No Design phase: the dependency_decision above is a version bump with an unchanged API surface at all 3 real call sites, not a new contract. Per the Orchestrator's loop, Design is only for runs that introduce a schema change, a new endpoint, or a shared type change — none apply here.

Phase 2 (devops) is gated on Phase 1's reviewer approval because bumping .nvmrc changes what `node-version-file: .nvmrc` resolves to for every future CI run and every contributor's `nvm use 20`-shaped habit — it must not land until the dependency it activates has already been proven, under Node 24, to load, migrate, transact and back up exactly as before.

CI itself needs no line changed in .github/workflows/ci.yml: both jobs already read `node-version-file: .nvmrc`, so bumping .nvmrc alone repoints CI at Node 24. Phase 2's devops task still opens the /update-ci skill and does a scratch-clone dry run of the CI steps under Node 24, per that skill's own guidance to verify locally before trusting a workflow file (or its absence of changes) to a push.

phases.name: Prove better-sqlite3 works unchanged under Node 24
phases.ships: The database layer (schema init/migration, all CRUD/transaction call sites, and the online-backup path) is verified end-to-end under a real Node 24 process in a scratch clone, with the dependency bumped and zero call-site code changes — nothing in the live checkout's runtime requirement has changed yet, so this phase is safe to land even before the repo declares Node 24 required.

phases.name: Declare and enforce Node 24 as the required runtime
phases.ships: Cloning the repo fresh and running `nvm use` now gets Node 24; `package.json` (root and client) declare it via `engines`; CI is confirmed (not just assumed) to pick up the same version and pass. This is the phase the acceptance bar's 'CI passes on Node 24' and '`package.json` must declare Node 24 support via engines' actually land in.

tasks.title: Bump better-sqlite3 to a Node-24-compatible release and verify all call sites in a scratch clone
tasks.goal: In root package.json, bump `better-sqlite3` from `^9.4.3` to `^12.11.1` and `@types/better-sqlite3` from `^7.6.8` to `^9.6.0` (devDependencies). No other dependency changes. Do this and all verification in a scratch clone of the repo (`cp -r` or `git worktree` into scratch, never this checkout — this checkout's dist/, client/dist/, flights.db and running :3000 server must stay untouched). The only files this task should end up diffing in the real checkout are `package.json` and `package-lock.json`; everything under src/db/*.ts, src/backup.ts, src/kmlExport.ts and src/auth/password.ts needs no code change (confirmed: better-sqlite3's API surface used here — prepare/get/all/run, transaction(), pragma() including the {simple:true} form, exec(), the async db.backup(), db.open — has had no breaking change across 9.x->12.x per WiseLibs/better-sqlite3 maintainer statement). If verification surfaces an actual behavior difference despite that, fix it minimally in the same file and note it explicitly in the report — do not silently paper over a real regression.
acceptance_criteria: In a scratch clone (not this checkout), `nvm install 24 >/dev/null 2>&1; nvm use 24; node -v` reports a v24.x.x, and `node -e "require('better-sqlite3')"` from within `node_modules` loads with no ABI/prebuild error after `npm ci` in that scratch clone.
`export NVM_DIR="$HOME/.nvm"; . "$NVM_DIR/nvm.sh"; nvm use 24; npx tsc --noEmit` (or `npm run test:types`) run inside the scratch clone exits 0.

`npm test` (Vitest) run under Node 24 in the scratch clone passes in full, including `tests/db/schema.test.ts` and `tests/backup.test.ts` specifically (the two suites exercising better-sqlite3 directly) and `tests/helpers/db.ts`'s scratch-db harness (createScratchDb/resetScratchDb/destroyScratchDb).

`npm run backup` (ts-node src/backup.ts) run under Node 24 against a scratch copy of a seeded database (never the live flights.db) produces a backup file that reopens with better-sqlite3 and passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` with no errors — this exercises the async `db.backup()` API path specifically.

A scratch server (built in the scratch clone with `npm run build`, started with `PORT=3100 FLIGHTS_DB_PATH=<scratch copy>` and its own working directory, never this checkout's dist/) boots under Node 24 with no addon-load error, and `curl http://localhost:3100/api/flights` (or equivalent read endpoint) returns HTTP 200; the scratch server is shut down by tracked PID at the end of the task, never by pkill-by-pattern.

This checkout's own `flights.db`/`flights.db-wal`/`flights.db-shm`, `dist/`, `client/dist/`, and the live server on port 3000 are byte-for-byte/mtime-unchanged before and after this task (state the check command and its output in the report).

`git diff --stat` in the real checkout shows changes only in `package.json` and `package-lock.json` (plus any of the three listed src/ files only if a real behavior gap was found and fixed, documented in the report).

tasks.title: Declare Node 24 as the required runtime in .nvmrc, package.json engines, and confirm CI
tasks.goal: Bump `.nvmrc` from `20` to `24`. Add `"engines": { "node": ">=24 <25" }` to root package.json (same style/level as the better-sqlite3 engines range researched in T-001-adjacent research — pin to the 24.x line, not open-ended). Add a matching `engines.node` entry to client/package.json for consistency (client build tooling runs under the same Node). Load the /update-ci skill before touching .github/workflows/ci.yml. Both CI jobs (build-and-test, e2e) already resolve their Node version via `node-version-file: .nvmrc`, so confirm via grep that no functional edit to ci.yml is required rather than assuming it — if you find a reason a line does need to change (e.g. a hardcoded Node version somewhere this task's own research missed), make the minimal edit and justify it explicitly in the report. Do not run `npm run build` or start any server in this checkout; all dry-run verification happens in a scratch clone.
acceptance_criteria: `cat .nvmrc` reads `24`.
`npm pkg get engines.node` (root) reports a range that includes 24.x and excludes 20.x and 26.x, e.g. `>=24 <25`.
`cd client && npm pkg get engines.node` reports a matching range.

`grep -n 'node-version-file' .github/workflows/ci.yml` shows both the build-and-test and e2e jobs still reading `.nvmrc` — report states explicitly whether ci.yml was left unchanged (expected) or what exact line changed and why.

Scratch-clone dry run of the CI steps under Node 24 (`nvm install 24` if not already present from T-001, `nvm use 24`): `npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm run test:types`, `npm test` all succeed at the repo root; `cd client && npm ci && npm run build && npm run test:types && npm test` all succeed — this is the local stand-in for `build-and-test` since Actions itself is not run from here.
This checkout's flights.db, dist/, client/dist/, and the live :3000 server remain untouched — state the before/after check.
